It is not a defect in the new code's own behavior — the new UI uses the new endpoints — but it is a specific, substantive backward-compatibility/migration risk for out-of-tree API consumers (silent no-op success on old PUT payloads, lost initial-members-on-create capability, no deprecation), which a maintainer would want to know before shipping. judged_text: The create/update request contract silently changed shape: nested `group` params, `usernames` on create, and the PATCH `changes` incremental-membership protocol were all removed, so existing API consumers now get 422s (create with old `group:` payload yields blank name) or silent no-op successes (PUT/PATCH with old payloads pass no top-level params, `group.save` runs, 200 is returned with nothing applied). Out-of-tree API consumers and scripts that create groups with initial members or patch membership incrementally get success responses while no membership change or group field is applied; there is no deprecation or version bump accompanying this rewrite.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes the admin groups API contract: `create` now reads top-level `params[:name]`/`params[:visible]` instead of nested `params[:group]` (and no longer accepts `usernames`), `update` now reads top-level params and removes the old PATCH incremental membership protocol (`update_patch` and `params[:changes]`), replacing membership edits with new `add_members`/`remove_member` endpoints and routes. This is a real, diff-grounded backward-incompatible change that can break existing consumers. However, parts of the finding overstate/are slightly inaccurate: `update` is not a pure no-op when old nested params are sent—it will still set `visible` to false when `params[:visible]` is missing—and `create` may error rather than succeed, depending on model validations not shown here. The core compatibility concern remains valid but is more of an API/deprecation issue than an inherent correctness defect within the new contract.
